description: The bar chart illustrates the annual number of hateful communication datasets published from 2012 to 2021, categorized by the number of languages they cover — either monolingual (“1”) or multilingual (“2+”) — as part of the systematic review “The Unseen Targets of Hate.” The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 100, with major gridlines at 10 and 100. The horizontal axis represents the year, spanning 2012 to 2021. Each year features two bars: a dark blue bar for datasets in one language and an orange bar for datasets in two or more languages. From 2012 to 2015, only monolingual datasets are present, with counts ranging from 1 to 3. Starting in 2016, the number of monolingual datasets begins to rise sharply, reaching 10 in 2016, 20 in 2017, 30 in 2018, 40 in 2019, 100 in 2020, and peaking at approximately 120 in 2021. Multilingual datasets appear in 2017 (around 5), dip in 2018 (around 2), rise to 7 in 2019, jump to 25 in 2020, and then fall to about 10 in 2021. A light blue bar appears in 2021 for monolingual datasets, possibly indicating a revised or separate count, and a small light orange bar appears for multilingual datasets in 2021. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of monolingual datasets over time, especially from 2019 onward, and the relatively smaller but growing presence of multilingual datasets.
